_note: C1 of 4 - viz units for R1 (the gene / transcript view), the isoform case study, and the gene/RBP side of search & browse. Every data_source names the exact file and columns. All sizes and counts are measured values from the survey. Baked artefacts are named as 'BAKE: data/...' and their upstream inputs given.

viz_units.name: Gene identity header
viz_units.what_it_shows: Gene symbol, product name, the RefSeq transcript being shown, its Ensembl crosswalk, and the four region lengths.
viz_units.encoding: Text block; the RefSeq id is monospace and copyable; ENSG/ENST render as small outlined chips.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE: data/gene/<SYMBOL>.json.gz, from motif_full_annotations.parquet (gene_symbol, sequence_id) + GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet (refseq_id_without_ver, 'Gene stable ID', 'Transcript stable ID', 'Gene stable ID version', 'Transcript stable ID version', transcript_length, len of utr5_sequence/cds_sequence/utr3_sequence/protein_sequence) + idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv (Entry, 'Protein names') for the product name. MUST drop_duplicates('refseq_id_without_ver') first (21,667 -> 19,210 rows; verified lossless).
interactions: click RefSeq -> copy
click ENSG/ENST -> copy
the transcript shown is always named explicitly because the table holds one transcript per gene

viz_units.name: Annotation-availability badge row
viz_units.what_it_shows: Four per-transcript availability flags so an empty panel is explained rather than looking broken: has_uniprot_accession (16,911/18,093 = 93.5%), has_domain_track (13,941/18,093 = 77.1%), has_rbp_peaks, has_utr_genome_coords (all UTR motifs).
viz_units.encoding: Four chips, filled with a check when present, hollow with a strike and a tooltip reason when absent.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE: data/gene/<SYMBOL>.json.gz field `avail`, computed from idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv (From -> Entry), annotation_results/annotated_protein_sequences.csv (RefSeq presence, 109,110 rows / 13,941 transcripts), data/processed/00.eclip/motif_rbp_overlaps.parquet (distinct motif ids), data/motif_genome_mappings_grch37.parquet (refseq_id_versionless).
interactions: hover an absent badge -> 'no UniProt accession resolves for this RefSeq (1,182 of 18,093 transcripts)'

viz_units.name: Transcript minimap (proportional 5'UTR-CDS-3'UTR bar with motif ticks)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The whole transcript to scale with every motif as a tick, so a reader sees motif density and distribution before scrolling into any sequence.
viz_units.encoding: One 100%-width SVG row, ~28px tall. Three background segments proportional to utr5/cds/utr3 lengths using REGION colours (#E69F00 / #009E73 / #A85A00) at 18% opacity. Each motif is a 2px-min tick at its scaled midpoint, coloured by the active colour-by channel. A protein sub-row sits beneath the CDS segment because protein coordinates are amino-acid units, not CDS nucleotides.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE: data/gene shard `motifs.{utr5,utr3,protein}[].{s,e,c}` from motif_full_annotations.parquet (region, motif_start, motif_end, motif_cluster); region lengths from the sequence parquet.
interactions: click a tick -> scroll that motif into view and pulse it
drag to brush a coordinate range -> filters the motif table
hover -> cluster id + position tooltip

viz_units.name: Region panel header with SeqScore and coverage
viz_units.what_it_shows: Per region: length, motif count, SeqScore (the mean of the NTScore array; UTRs only), and the fraction of bases covered by motifs.
viz_units.encoding: A sticky 32px bar in the REGION colour with the number set in tabular figures; the coverage fraction as a 60px inline meter with the population median marked as a reference tick (utr5 0.307, utr3 0.261, protein 0.288).
viz_units.data_source: SeqScore = mean of the per-nt array in outputs_utr3_score_0318.h5[<refseq>]['score'] and .../h5cache/outputs_utr5_score_0326.h5[<refseq>]['score'] (baked into the shard, so no h5 at runtime). Coverage computed at bake from motif_start/motif_end over region length.
interactions: collapse/expand the region panel
hover the coverage meter -> 'this transcript 0.31 · all transcripts p10 0.188 / p50 0.307 / p90 0.464'

viz_units.name: Sequence viewer lane (the core R1 unit)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The literal 5'UTR, 3'UTR or protein sequence with motif spans highlighted in place.
viz_units.encoding: Monospace text in a single flat lane. Run-length alternation of unhighlighted text nodes and motif <span>s - ONE element per segment, never per nucleotide. Measured: p50 89 / p99 279 / max 381 segments for all three regions of a page, versus p50 1,940 / max 7,784 per-nucleotide spans. Zero-overlap is proven (max stacking depth exactly 1 across all 53,367 transcript-region groups), so there is no lane packing. Line width is user-selectable (default 60); a left gutter carries the 1-based display coordinate of each line's first residue while all internal maths stays 0-based.
viz_units.data_source: Sequence from BAKE data/seq/<refseq>.json.gz (utr5/utr3/protein), originally GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet columns utr5_sequence, utr3_sequence, protein_sequence. Spans from the gene shard's motif arrays (motif_start, motif_end, motifs, motif_cluster, motif_score, motif_entropy, plddt).
interactions: click a span -> VU-C1-19 popover
select text -> copy in the displayed alphabet
hover -> the span's cluster id in the status line
keyboard: Tab cycles motif spans, Enter opens the popover (accessibility)
viz_units.critical_rule: highlight = seq.slice(m.s, m.e + 1); length = m.e - m.s + 1. Verified 889,215/889,215. Off-by-one here shifts every highlight in the site.

viz_units.name: Motif span element
viz_units.what_it_shows: One motif instance inside the sequence lane.
viz_units.encoding: Subtle background fill (12-18% alpha) with a 1px solid inset outline in the full-strength colour, plus 1px horizontal padding. EVERY span is individually bordered - 53,729 adjacent pairs abut exactly (gap 0) and 9,838 of those share a cluster, so without a separator they fuse into single false motifs. Colour comes from the active colour-by channel (module / cluster / region). Optional opacity modulated by motif_score (domain [-4.83, 0], always negative). Protein spans longer than 60 aa (protein motif max is 535 aa, median 8) render with a hatched middle and a length badge instead of a solid fill, so one instance cannot swallow the panel.
viz_units.data_source: gene shard motif objects: s, e, seq, c (motif_cluster), sc (motif_score), en (motif_entropy), plddt, ann
interactions: click -> popover
hover -> outline thickens and the same motif's row in the table highlights (bidirectional linking)

viz_units.name: Coordinate ruler / gutter
viz_units.what_it_shows: Position along the region, with tens ticks and hundreds labels.
viz_units.encoding: A thin SVG strip above each sequence lane aligned to the monospace grid via the measured character advance; left gutter repeats the line-start coordinate. Displays 1-based positions with a footnote that stored coordinates are 0-based inclusive.
viz_units.data_source: derived from sequence length in the shard
interactions: click a tick -> copies the coordinate
the ruler is the drop target for the minimap brush

viz_units.name: NTScore area track (5'UTR and 3'UTR)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The manuscript's central per-nucleotide quantity - the conditional log-probability of the observed base - as a continuous profile directly above the sequence it belongs to. This is what makes the gene page a new object rather than a coloured-text viewer.
viz_units.encoding: Filled area chart, 44px tall, x aligned 1:1 with the sequence lane's character grid. y domain [-4, 0] (real range roughly -4 to 0; SOX2 3'UTR mean -1.196, min -3.984, max -0.045), zero at the top. Fill uses a sequential ramp; the region's own mean (SeqScore) is drawn as a dashed reference line. Motif spans are echoed as faint vertical bands so the reader can see whether a motif sits on a score peak.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/data/outputs_utr3_score_0318.h5 (18,585 RefSeq groups, each with 'score' and 'entropy' float32 arrays) and /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/explore_biology/01.protein_localization/analysis/data/h5cache/outputs_utr5_score_0326.h5 (18,093 keys, exactly the motif-table transcripts). Array length is verified 1:1 with the region sequence for every transcript tested. BAKE: int8-quantised into data/seq/<refseq>.json.gz; never ship the 169.5 MB h5.
interactions: hover -> exact NTScore at that position
brush -> selects a coordinate range and filters the motif table
toggle a second series for 'entropy' from the same h5
viz_units.library: none (path built from a typed array)
viz_units.render_tech: SVG for <=2,000 nt, Canvas above that (3'UTR max is 7,601 nt; only 587 transcripts exceed 5,000 nt)

viz_units.name: NTScore colour key and scale note
viz_units.what_it_shows: The y domain, the units, and the honest statement that no per-nucleotide score exists for the protein or the CDS.
viz_units.encoding: A 120x14 gradient swatch with -4 and 0 labelled, plus one line of caption text.
viz_units.data_source: static copy + the domain constant in data/theme.json
interactions: the caption links to the glossary NTScore entry

viz_units.name: pLDDT track (protein panel only)
viz_units.what_it_shows: AlphaFold predicted local structure confidence per motif - the protein panel's analogue of the UTR NTScore track, and the visual encoding of the ordered-vs-IDR story.
viz_units.encoding: A stepped bar lane, one bar per protein motif (NOT a continuous track - the value exists only per motif). Domain [0, 1] - NOT 0-100. Population reference ticks at p10 0.376 and p50 0.801. Diverging ramp with the low end tinted toward the IDR accent so a disordered motif is visible at a glance (SOX2's HMG-box motif at aa 52-59 is 0.980; its N-terminal disordered motif at aa 0-5 is 0.320).
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column plddt (254,466 non-null, all region=='protein'; 0 for utr3/utr5), baked into the gene shard.
interactions: hover -> exact pLDDT and the motif it belongs to
click -> selects that motif

viz_units.name: InterPro domain ruler (protein panel)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Real InterPro domain intervals under the protein sequence, so 'this motif sits inside domain X' is visible rather than asserted.
viz_units.encoding: Horizontal capsules on 1-3 stacked rows (domains DO overlap, unlike motifs, so this lane needs real interval packing - the only place in the app that does). Colour by InterPro entry type (family / domain / homologous_superfamily / conserved_site / repeat / active_site / binding_site / ptm).
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_annotation/sequence_annotation_human/annotation_results/annotated_protein_sequences.csv (109,110 rows, 13,941 RefSeq ids, columns interpro_label, interpro_description, start, end, Length, Entry, 'Entry Name'; start/end non-null on 100% of rows; mean 7.83 domains per transcript, max 436) joined to /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/interpro_entry_map.csv (ipr, name, type, go_ids, go_names) for type and GO.
interactions: hover -> IPR accession, name, type, GO names
click -> deep link to interpro.ebi.ac.uk/entry/InterPro/<ipr>
the lane renders a 'no domain track for this transcript' state for the 4,152 transcripts (22.9%) with no row

viz_units.name: UniProt feature track (typed)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Typed, coordinate-accurate UniProt features under the protein sequence - Chain, Domain, Region, Helix, Beta strand, Transmembrane, Modified residue, Disulfide bond, Compositional bias, Natural variant, Topological domain.
viz_units.encoding: Grouped lanes, one row per feature type, ordered structure-first (Helix / Beta strand / Turn) then functional. Features with an empty description are labelled by their TYPE rather than dropped - 516,709 of 1,577,512 features carry no text and the shipped aggregation silently discarded them, hiding 39,189 Helix and 30,854 Beta strand motif hits.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_annotation/sequence_annotation_human/data/processed/03.uniprot/uniprot_annotation.parquet (1,577,512 features, 195,761 accessions, 35 types; columns type, start, end, description), joined per transcript via data/idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv (From, Entry, Reviewed) preferring Reviewed=='reviewed' (covers 16,045 sequence_ids, only 46 ambiguous). BAKE re-runs the overlap with 0-based-corrected coordinates -> 756,192 hits over 231,439 motifs (90.95%), mean 3.27 features/motif.
interactions: type-row show/hide
hover -> type, description, coordinates
click -> uniprot.org/uniprotkb/<Entry>#<feature>
viz_units.note: NEVER comma-split motif_full_annotations.uniprot_annotations - it is wrong for 6.894% of annotated protein motifs and produces artifact tokens such as ' mitochondrial' (3,544 occurrences).

viz_units.name: MobiDB disorder / LIP / phase-separation track
viz_units.what_it_shows: Per-residue disorder intervals under the protein sequence, instead of a list of 87 opaque term names.
viz_units.encoding: A stippled band lane. Defaults to curated + derived evidence only; prediction and homology evidence are behind a toggle (on protein rows the split is prediction 686,986 / homology 299,358 / derived 141,052 / curated 21,463 entries). Term names are parsed by their 4-level evidence-feature-source grammar and rendered as 'phase separation (curated)' style labels.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_annotation/sequence_annotation_human/data/raw_annotations/06.mobidb/mobidb_search_2026-05-13T19-55-12.tsv (1,269,524 rows: UniProt ACC, term, comma-joined 'start..end' ranges, content_fraction, content_count, length) keyed by the Entry column in data/processed/06.mobidb/motif_mobidb_annotations.parquet.
interactions: evidence-level toggle (curated / derived / homology / prediction)
hover -> term, evidence class, source database
viz_units.note: PROTEIN ROWS ONLY. The unmasked column is populated on 67.0% of 5'UTR and 25.3% of 3'UTR rows with protein disorder terms (209,959 spurious rows) because the builder never filtered region.

viz_units.name: eCLIP peak lane
viz_units.what_it_shows: Which RBPs have an eCLIP peak overlapping each UTR motif, as its own track rather than merged into a generic 'RBP' field.
viz_units.encoding: A 12px lane of segments aligned to motif positions, labelled with up to 3 RBP names and a '+N' overflow chip. Segment opacity by peak count.
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column RBPs_eCLIP (list<str>, 145,814 filled = 22.19% of utr3 and 26.36% of utr5 rows; 150 distinct names; mean 2.68 per annotated motif, max 38), enriched at bake with peak counts, cell lines and score range from data/processed/00.eclip/motif_rbp_overlaps.parquet (2,671,559 overlaps, columns peak_id, RBP_name, score, method, sample; 19 cell lines).
interactions: click a segment -> the RBP evidence drawer (peak count, distinct cell lines, score range, POSTAR3 peak ids)
filter the lane by cell line - something no static figure can offer

viz_units.name: PAR-CLIP/PARalyzer peak lane
viz_units.what_it_shows: Same, for the PAR-CLIP method - kept separate because the methods barely agree.
viz_units.encoding: identical lane style, distinct method badge colour
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column 'RBPs_PAR-CLIP,PARalyzer' (list<str>, 262,932 filled = 46.27% utr3 / 20.43% utr5; 57 distinct names; mean 3.55, max 40). Top values ATXN2 115,724; ELAVL1 93,426; TARDBP 71,865; HNRNPC 63,575; LIN28B 53,311.
interactions: as VU-C1-14

viz_units.name: iCLIP/Piranha peak lane
viz_units.what_it_shows: Same, for iCLIP with Piranha_0.01 peak calling.
viz_units.encoding: identical lane style
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column 'RBPs_iCLIP,Piranha_0.01' (79,144 filled = 12.41% utr3 / 12.74% utr5; 32 distinct names; mean 1.98, max 27). NOTE this method's names need the alias map: U2AF65->U2AF2, TDP43->TARDBP, UNR->CSDE1, IMP3->IGF2BP3, HNRNPH->HNRNPH1.
interactions: as VU-C1-14; alias-corrected names show the original POSTAR3 label on hover

viz_units.name: iCLIP/CIMS peak lane
viz_units.what_it_shows: Same, for iCLIP with CIMS.
viz_units.encoding: identical lane style
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column 'RBPs_iCLIP,CIMS' (135,564 filled = 21.59% utr3 / 20.36% utr5; 22 distinct names; mean 1.79, max 19). Top DDX3X 58,902; HNRNPC 21,476; CSTF2 19,923; UPF1 19,255; PTBP1 18,861.
interactions: as VU-C1-14

viz_units.name: miRNA target-site lane (3'UTR only)
viz_units.what_it_shows: TargetScan predicted miRNA family sites overlapping 3'UTR motifs.
viz_units.encoding: A sparse lane of small diamonds - deliberately sparse-looking, because only 4.698% of 3'UTR motifs carry one. The lane header prints that coverage number so the sparseness reads as a fact, not a rendering failure.
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column mirna_annotations_targetscan (24,251 filled overall; 24,228 on utr3 = 4.698%, 23 on utr5; 219 distinct families; mean 1.31, max 10). Optional enrichment with per-site score and site type by re-joining /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_annotation/sequence_annotation_human/data/raw_annotations/04.targetscan/TargetScan_Predicted_Target_Locations.default_predictions.hg19.bed (126,699 sites, name/score/strand/itemRgb) through data/motif_genome_mappings_grch37.parquet.
interactions: hover -> family string (e.g. 'miR-15-5p/16-5p/195-5p/424-5p/497-5p')
click -> #/browse/mirna/<family>
link out to TargetScan by family name and gene symbol

viz_units.name: Motif callout popover
viz_units.what_it_shows: Everything about one motif instance, in a card anchored to its span: id, coordinates, sequence (in the displayed alphabet), cluster + its name, module, the three score numbers, the PWM-match bits, and every annotation chip grouped by source with its overlap rule.
viz_units.encoding: Card ~360px. A miniature score triple (motif_score / entropy / pLDDT) rendered as three 40px bullet bars against their population distributions - a tooltip that is really a mini-chart.
viz_units.data_source: gene shard motif object; cluster name and module from BAKE data/clusters_index.json; PWM-match bits from BAKE L1/instance_match.parquet (keyed on raw_motif_index, computed with coverage() from 16_consensus_repertoire.py, COV_BITS=0.5).
interactions: 'open cluster' -> #/cluster/<id>
'see in network' -> #/network?level=clusters&focus=<id>
'add to basket'
Esc closes; the popover is keyboard-reachable

viz_units.name: Per-gene motif table
viz_units.what_it_shows: All of this transcript's motifs as a sortable, filterable, exportable table - the tabular counterpart of the highlight layer.
viz_units.encoding: Dense table: region, position, sequence, cluster (with a 24px inline logo), module chip, motif_score micro-bar, PWM bits, annotation chips. Median gene has 43 motifs; p99 142; max 336 (CYFIP1) - so a virtualised body is used above 150 rows.
viz_units.data_source: gene shard motifs arrays; per-cluster name/logo from data/clusters_index.json and data/logos.json
interactions: sort by any column (default: region then position)
row hover highlights the corresponding span in the sequence lane and vice versa
click -> scroll to and pulse the span
export CSV/JSON with provenance columns

viz_units.name: Annotation chip row
viz_units.what_it_shows: One motif's annotations as source-grouped chips, each carrying (a) its source database, (b) the overlap rule used, (c) an evidence count where available.
viz_units.encoding: Small rounded chips; source encoded by a 3px left border colour keyed to the RNA/protein layer split in annotation_coverage_stats.json. Chips for structural UniProt types show the type rather than an empty label.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE L1/motifs_master.parquet normalised annotation block. Overlap rules differ per database and are shown, not assumed: InterPro = any overlap (0-based converted); UniProt and ELM = any overlap (1-based raw); MobiDB = motif fully CONTAINED (0-based half-open); IDPO = contained (1-based); SignalP = any overlap.
interactions: hover -> the overlap rule sentence and the source's overall coverage percentage
click -> the source's browse facet or an external deep link

viz_units.name: RBP chip with method-agreement badge
viz_units.what_it_shows: One RBP, plus how many of the four CLIP methods support it - a free, honest confidence axis.
viz_units.encoding: Chip with a 4-segment micro-badge; filled segments = supporting methods. Population distribution printed in the tooltip: over 634,749 UTR motifs, 308,753 have 0 methods, 144,288 exactly 1, 95,096 two, 57,474 three, 29,138 all four.
viz_units.data_source: the four list columns of motif_full_annotations.parquet unioned per motif after alias normalisation; peak-level evidence from data/processed/00.eclip/motif_rbp_overlaps.parquet (peak_id, score, method, sample).
interactions: hover -> methods, peak count, distinct cell lines, score range
click -> #/browse/rbp/<name>
the tooltip carries the mandatory semantics sentence: 'genes carrying this motif also tend to carry this RBP's peak in the same UTR' - fold is an upper bound for CLIP sources

viz_units.name: Gene module fingerprint bar
viz_units.what_it_shows: How this gene's motifs distribute across the six modules and the no-module state - the R1 -> R3 bridge.
viz_units.encoding: A 100%-width stacked bar segmented by module colour, with an explicit hatched 'no module' segment. Beneath it, per-region mini-bars. For SOX2 this correctly reads 43 of 47 instances in M1 clusters (12 protein, 22 utr3, 9 utr5) and 3 in M2 - all three in the 5'UTR.
viz_units.data_source: gene shard motif clusters mapped through BAKE data/clusters_index.json module field (derived once from /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v4_0621/03.interacting_modules/modules.json). Module membership at the GENE level (a different, stricter definition) from module_gene_members/module_gene_index.csv (module_id, gene_symbol, refseq_ids, n_sig_terms_hit, n_trusted_terms_hit) - covering 8,846 of 18,093 transcripts (48.9%).
interactions: click a segment -> filters the highlight layer to that module's motifs
the 'no module' segment opens the VU-C1-35 explainer
the gene-level vs motif-level distinction is a labelled toggle, because they are different definitions and confusing them is the commonest misreading
viz_units.note: Expect ~45% of a typical gene's motifs to have no module - 486,307 of 889,215 instances (54.7%) are in module-assigned clusters. The legend states this so it does not read as a bug.

viz_units.name: Colour-by selector
viz_units.what_it_shows: Which categorical channel drives the motif highlight colours: module / cluster / region / score.
viz_units.encoding: Segmented control; the legend below it changes with the selection and always prints the count of uncoloured items in the current mode.
viz_units.data_source: data/theme.json palettes
interactions: changing the mode re-renders class names only - no refetch and no relayout

viz_units.name: Motif filter chip bar
viz_units.what_it_shows: Density controls, needed from day one: the median gene carries 21 3'UTR + 11 protein + 5 5'UTR motifs and the max 3'UTR count is 182.
viz_units.encoding: A row of toggle chips with live counts: module (7 values incl. none), annotated-only (36.1% of instances have no annotation at all), minimum motif_score slider, cluster picker, minimum length, has-CLIP-support.
viz_units.data_source: gene shard fields; counts computed client-side
interactions: filters apply simultaneously to the sequence highlights, the minimap ticks and the table
filter state goes into the URL

viz_units.name: RNA/DNA alphabet toggle
viz_units.what_it_shows: UTR sequences as RNA (U, default, matching the manuscript) or DNA (T, matching storage).
viz_units.encoding: Small two-state switch in each UTR panel header; disabled and hidden on the protein panel.
viz_units.data_source: client-side transliteration of the shard sequence; storage is verified DNA-only (utr5 and utr3 motif and sequence alphabets are exactly ['A','C','G','T'], zero U)
interactions: toggling rewrites the text nodes only
the search box accepts both forms and normalises U->T before matching, so a reader typing the paper's own UCAUC / UCUCC / GCCACC gets hits
viz_units.note: MUST NOT apply to the protein panel: U there is selenocysteine (the protein alphabet is the 20 aa plus U).

viz_units.name: Line-wrap width control
viz_units.what_it_shows: Characters per line (30 / 60 / 90 / fit).
viz_units.encoding: Small select in the region header; 'fit' measures the container and the monospace advance.
viz_units.data_source: none
interactions: changing width re-flows the lane and re-aligns the ruler, the NTScore track and every annotation lane in one pass

viz_units.name: Gene export control (FASTA / CSV / JSON)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Download exactly what is on screen.
viz_units.encoding: A small ⤓ menu: FASTA of the three sequences (with the displayed alphabet), CSV of the motif table with provenance columns, or the raw shard JSON.
viz_units.data_source: the in-memory shard; a client-side Blob, no server
interactions: respects the active filters, and says so ('20 of 20 motifs' / '6 of 20 motifs, filtered')

viz_units.name: Transcript picker
viz_units.what_it_shows: The other transcripts of a multi-transcript gene.
viz_units.encoding: A dropdown, shown ONLY for the 215 of 17,847 genes (1.20%) that have more than one transcript. Distribution {1:17632, 2:193, 3:17, 4:3, 5:1, 7:1}; the maximum is BAG6 with 7, then DDR1 5, then HLA-DRB1 / RPS9 / VPS52 4.
viz_units.data_source: search_index.json.gz symbol -> [{sequence_id, n_motifs}]
interactions: switching transcript reloads the shard and preserves region/filter state

viz_units.name: motif_score micro-bar
viz_units.what_it_shows: One motif's model score against the population distribution.
viz_units.encoding: A 40x8 bullet bar. Domain is NEGATIVE: min -4.831, p25 -1.438, p50 -1.135, p75 -0.858, max ~0. The population median is a reference tick. Any colour scale must be built for a negative domain.
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column motif_score
interactions: hover -> exact value and percentile

viz_units.name: motif_entropy micro-bar
viz_units.what_it_shows: Per-motif entropy against the population (min 0.0, p50 1.179, max 2.947).
viz_units.encoding: as VU-C1-30
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column motif_entropy
interactions: hover -> exact value and percentile

viz_units.name: PWM-match bits badge
viz_units.what_it_shows: How well this specific instance matches its own cluster's consensus - the difference between 'this gene is in the cluster' and 'this gene actually carries the motif'.
viz_units.encoding: A small numeric badge (bits/position) plus a tier letter: A (the called instance IS the literal motif at the same position), C (consensus carrier only), L (literal only). Threshold 0.5 bits/pos, the same COV_BITS the published coverage numbers use.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE L1/instance_match.parquet, computed by sliding each cluster's top PWM (from consensus_repertoire.pkl / the refill) over each member string with coverage() from motif_pair_network/16_consensus_repertoire.py. Definition and worked numbers from motif_pair_network/m4_motif_examples/README.md and m4_motif_instances.csv (columns consensus, cid, cluster, region, gene, refseq, instance, matched_window, match_start, bits, exact, clip).
interactions: hover -> the matched window, the offset, the bits, and the three-tier definition
viz_units.note: This is what stops R1 and R3 disagreeing: of 1,988 M4 member transcripts only 106 are both literal and carrier and only 53 are tier A.

viz_units.name: Co-carrier suggestion strip
viz_units.what_it_shows: Other genes that carry the same motif-cluster pair as this gene - the narrative nudge from one gene to its cohort.
viz_units.encoding: A horizontal strip of up to 12 gene chips with a count, per gated pair this gene participates in.
viz_units.data_source:
BAKE data/graph/edge_genes/

~.json, precomputed as a bitwise AND of one Pc column and one Uc column of motif_pair_network/intermediate/consensus_presence.npz (Pc 18,068x275 bool, Uc 18,068x951 bool, aligned arrays genes, p_cid, u_cid, p_cluster, u_cluster, pmod, umod, p_consensus, u_consensus, p_cov, u_cov).
interactions: click a chip -> that gene with the same two clusters pre-highlighted
'see all N' -> the edge drawer's carrier list

viz_units.name: Missing-region empty state
viz_units.what_it_shows: That a region has zero motifs, with the population number, and the sequence still shown.
viz_units.encoding: An inline notice bar inside the region panel; the sequence renders unhighlighted below it. NEVER hide the panel.
viz_units.data_source: counts from the gene shard; population figures baked in: 808 transcripts have no 5'UTR motifs, 87 no 3'UTR motifs, 17 no protein motifs; only 17,191 of 18,093 (95.0%) have all three.
interactions: links to the About-the-data gaps register

viz_units.name: No-module explainer
viz_units.what_it_shows: Why a motif or a gene has no module - stated as a scientific result, not a hole.
viz_units.encoding: A short bordered card with the reason and the numbers, plus a link to the gate.
viz_units.data_source: static copy bound to measured numbers: 387 of 900 clusters (102 prot, 251 utr3, 34 utr5) and 9,247 of 18,093 transcripts (51.1%) have no module; 2,620 of 180,000 pairs passed.
interactions: 'show its best sub-threshold partners' expands VU-C2-38

viz_units.name: Genome-coordinate link-out
viz_units.what_it_shows: The genomic position of a UTR motif, for UCSC / IGV.
viz_units.encoding: A small chip on UTR motif popovers only (no equivalent exists for protein-region motifs).
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/data/motif_genome_mappings_grch37.parquet (634,749 rows = all utr3+utr5 motifs; columns refseq_id_versionless, accession e.g. NC_000008.10, strand, transcript_motif_start/end, motif_genomic_segments, motif_genomic_start/end, mapping_note). A GRCh38 twin exists at motif_genome_mappings_grch38.parquet.
interactions: assembly switch GRCh37/GRCh38
copy as chr:start-end
open in UCSC

viz_units.name: Isoform notice
viz_units.what_it_shows: That the portal holds one transcript per gene, and - for the five genes where isoform data exists - a link to the case study.
viz_units.encoding: A one-line notice under the header; upgraded to a link for CD47, CD44 and BIRC3.
viz_units.data_source: static copy + the key list of figure2/elavl1_isoform_tracks/data/all_utr3_scores.npz (BIRC3-LU/SU, CD44-LU/SU, CD47-LU/SU)
interactions: link -> V17

viz_units.name: Gene search-result row with motif sparkbar
viz_units.what_it_shows: A gene, its transcript, and its motif composition at a glance.
viz_units.encoding: Symbol + RefSeq + a 60px three-segment stacked bar (utr5 / protein / utr3) in REGION colours, scaled to the p95 total so dense genes are visibly dense. Motifs per gene: p50 43, p90 93, p99 142, max 336 (CYFIP1).
viz_units.data_source: BAKE data/search_index.json.gz: gene_symbol -> [{sequence_id, n_utr5, n_prot, n_utr3, n_total, module_mask}] (measured 0.91 MB raw / 0.157 MB gz for all 17,847 symbols + 18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST)
interactions: keyboard navigable
Enter -> #/gene/<sym>
shows a module chip strip if the gene is in module_gene_index.csv (8,720 of 17,847 symbols)

viz_units.name: RBP facet row with method badges
viz_units.what_it_shows: One of the 203 RBP names, which of the four CLIP methods report it, how many motifs it annotates, and its alias if the name is non-standard.
viz_units.encoding: Name + 4-segment method badge + motif count bar + optional alias warning. Only 4 RBPs (CSTF2, HNRNPC, IGF2BP3, TARDBP) appear in all four methods; 166 of 203 appear in exactly one.
viz_units.data_source: the four RBP list columns of motif_full_annotations.parquet, exploded and counted at bake; alias map is a hand-curated ~15-row CSV shipped in the portal (U2AF65->U2AF2, TDP43->TARDBP, UNR->CSDE1, IMP3->IGF2BP3, HNRNPH->HNRNPH1, plus the opaque labels 'ACI' 4,960 entries and 'SDOS' which are flagged as unresolved).
interactions: click -> #/browse/rbp/<name> listing its clusters and genes
hover the alias warning -> the original POSTAR3 label

viz_units.name: Paired isoform NTScore comparator
viz_units.what_it_shows: Long-3'UTR versus short-3'UTR NTScore profiles for the same gene, aligned at the stop codon - the Fig 2g comparison.
viz_units.encoding: Two stacked area tracks sharing an x scale anchored at position 0, with an optional difference track (LU minus SU over the shared region).
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure2/elavl1_isoform_tracks/data/all_utr3_scores.npz (9 arrays keyed BIRC3-LU/BIRC3-SU/CD44-LU/CD44-SU/CD47-LU/CD47-SU)
interactions: gene selector
shared brush
difference-track toggle
